- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% relative to model output.
- Underestimate late in the horizon; adjust final 5–10 days upward by 1–2% to align with observed mean reversion toward recent high levels.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce subsequent forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overshoot.
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce forecast peak by 2–4% and shift downward slope to match observed decay.
- For 30-day forecasts, apply a 1–2% downward bias to the first 10 days if recent history shows volatility or downward momentum.
- If true outcome is consistently 2–3% higher than forecast for 5+ days, apply a 1–2% upward adjustment to the model’s mean forecast for the remainder of the horizon.
